Projects.Title: AHEPA Website Redesign
Projects.Desc: I volunteered to redesign the website for the Ottawa chapter of AHEPA to help them modernize their online presence and continue their mission of promoting Hellenism in Ottawa. I collaborated with stakeholders to determine necessary functionality, provided various design alternatives in Figma, redesigned the website layout and structure with the Square Online platform, provided refinements from stakeholder feedback, and compiled documentation for future upkeep.

Image.alt: The site is managed through Square and was redesigned using the Square Online platform. The site now provides easy-to-navigate information about AHEPA's mission, events and membership, and more.
Design alternatives for the site banner, colour schemes and fonts were provided to stakeholders through Figma.
Mockups of site pages were created in Figma to satisfy the site requirements.
Documentation was provided to stakeholders outlining key features and common pitfalls of the Square Online platform for future upkeep.

Projects.Title: The Little Robot
Projects.Desc: The Little Robot is a linear 3D platforming and melee combat game where you play as a small robot trapped in an isolated testing facility, unaware of the world beyond its walls. This game was created with 5 peers as our final year 8-month Capstone project in Unity. As the team lead, I took on the infrastructure of the game including scene management and checkpoints. I was also responsible for the majority of the environmental scripting such as the conveyor belts, moving platforms, and vent systems. I was also responsible for creating the cutscenes sequences and implementing the (many) cameras using the Cinemachine plugin.

Image.alt: The robot must traverse through platforming sections as he descends deeper into the facility.
Explore a mysterious facility where dangerous fungus runs rampant.
The robot must defeat a dangerous reoccuring enemy with its fast-paced attacks.

Projects.Title: Portfolio
Projects.Desc: I started to create this portfolio website in my 3rd year of university to showcase some of the cool academic and personal projects I've been working on. I created it using component-driven React.js as which I learned throughout university and at a co-op placement. Initially created with CSS, it has since been updated to use Tailwind. I will be continuing to update this portfolio as I create more projects and learn new skills!

Image.alt: This portfolio showcases a bit about me! A continuous work in progress, I plan to keep adding to it!
I created a custom theme component to allow for a dark mode and light mode. This is one of the tasks I took on during my co-op placement to improve their React application.

Projects.Title: Crab Cove
Projects.Desc: Crab Cove is a relaxing game about a crab collecting items to decorate his sandcastle! Created by 3 peers and I to fulfill the challenge of making a unique player controller for our 4th year Advanced Game Dev course in Unity, I was responsible for developing the crab's sideways movement and item spawning with C#, as well as the camerawork with the Cinemachine plugin.

Image.alt: Help the crab collect treasures for his home!
The crab can dig holes in the sand to find various items.
The crab can pick up items with either claw to bring them back to his sandcastle home and decorate it.

Projects.Title: Garden Planner
Projects.Desc: The Garden Planner was created as the term project for my 4th year Web Frameworks course. The goal was to create a useful application with a django backend and a React frontend. Because of my interest in gardening, I decided to create a garden planner that allows users to plan out their gardens by specifying the dimensions and amount of sun and using the external OpenFarm API to suggest possible plants to grow. Users can then save these plants to their gardens and be notified when they should be watered and harvested. User accounts are also saved to the database so that users can login and logout at any time.

Image.alt: Users can create and update garden specifications from the main page.
Viewing a garden allows users to see the existing plants and see possible new ones that fit the garden criteria from the OpenFarm API.
Users can view all of the notifications from their gardens.
Users can create accounts to login and logout of the application.

Projects.Title: Hangman
Projects.Desc: As a way to teach myself React.js, I created a game of hangman. The first iteration I made to prepare for my university co-ops and it was a semi-functional and poorly structured program. It has since been remade with React best practices. The game leverages the Wikipedia API to provide the player with a random Wikipedia article title to guess. The UI is heavily influenced by the video game Persona 5, which also makes use of tarot cards like the Hanged Man.

Image.alt: All English letters (Aa-Zz) are hidden from the player. Any irregular letters, numbers, or punctuation characters are shown.
Players can choose to play on 3 difficulty modes. Easy is the default and allows 10 incorrect guesses before a game over, Hard allows 5 guesses and None allows infinite.
Once the title has been successfully guessed, or a game over is triggered, the player is able to travel to the corresponding Wikipedia article.

Projects.Title: OC Transpo Redesign
Projects.Desc: A peer and I were tasked with analysing and redesigning a website for our 4th year UX Experience and Accessibility course. We chose the OC Transpo site as it is a frequently used service for university students and the site had many areas for improvement. We conducted user surveys and accessibility checks to find pain points, brainstormed to create mid-fidelity mockups in Figma and documented the process in a written report.

Image.alt: The existing site was analyzed using the WAVE accessibility checker and various screen readers after which a detailed document of errors and warnings was written.
User survey and think-aloud sessions were conducted with university-age participants to identify the strengths and weaknesses of the existing site.
New designs were drawn with pen and paper to resolve the main issues found in the analysis phase.
Mid-fidelity mockups of several key pages were created in Figma to demonstrate the new design.

Projects.Title: Nature Museum Whale App
Projects.Desc: 3 peers and I were tasked with creating an interactive application to better immerse visitors at the Canadian Museum of Nature. Our idea was to create an app that would lead users to certain exhibits via an AR whale on the screen and progressively louder whale calls as they got close to the exhibit. We conducted significant user testing and analysis before brainstorming suitable design alternatives. A low fidelity design was created in Figma and tested with users before creating a mid-fidelity prototype.

Image.alt: User survey and think-aloud sessions were conducted with users of various ages to identify what features would be most engaging. User personas and scenarios were also created to better understand our target audience.
Initial designs were drawn with pen and paper to satisfy the criteria of the user tests.
Low-fidelity mockups of the app design were created in Figma before being tested again by users.
A final mid-fidelity prototype was created based on the low-fidelity feedback.
Our mid-fidelity prototype was created in Figma and shown to the many users we tested throughout the process.

Projects.Title: Persona 3 Background
Projects.Desc: A computer background created using Vue.js and deployed to Wallpaper Engine. Initially created using vanilla JavaScript a few years ago, I decided to recreate it with Vue to improve the cleanliness of the code. The goal of this project was to imitate the UI from the video game Persona 3 Portable, one of my personal favourites. This background displays the current date, the time of day, the phase of the moon and indicates how many days are left until a full moon. The background images are pulled directly from the PSP version's game files.

Image.alt: After School is one of the times of day listed in the UI (the game characters attend high school). Others include Morning, Lunch, Evening and Late Night.
More memorable phases of the moon, such as Quarter, Half and Full moons are spelled out directly. Other moon phases have the number of days until a full moon beside it.
Notable times of day and background images are different during weekends.
Following with the game, the 'hidden hour' after midnight changes the UI to green. As an extra hour per day does not exist in real life, this occurs between midnight and 1am.

Projects.Title: Event Scheduler
Projects.Desc: This Proof-of-Concept mobile application was created as an individual assignment for my 4th year Mobile App Development course. The goal was to create an event scheduler that allows users to view, add, update, delete events, and notify users of upcoming events. Multiple early designs that fit the specifications along with standard mobile app design theories were considered. The final design was then created using Android Studio with Java. As a proof of concept, the app is not fully functional, but it does demonstrate the intended design and functionality, including multiple pages with Android Fragments, and data storage with ViewModels.

Image.alt: Many designs were drawn out on paper, and the best few were created as wireframes in Balsamiq.
The wireframe designs were put into a predictive modelling program to estimate task times.
The final design was created in Android Studio and tested with a virtual device.

Projects.Title: Flower Flux
Projects.Desc: Help Gatsbee the bee pollinate the flowers in his garden! 3 peers and I created this 2D side-scrolling game in our Intro to Game Dev course in 2nd year with Unity. I was responsible for the side scrolling, the UI and menu scripting as well as the pollination ability.

Image.alt: Fly around as Gatsbee to each of your flowers and pollinate them.
A simple game where players must juggle the timers of each flower to prevent them from dying.
Each level adds new flowers of increasing pollen difficulties!

Projects.Title: Crow Game & Controller
Projects.Desc: A peer and I were tasked with creating a game and a custom controller using Arduino and it's StandardFirmata library along with the C++ openFrameworks Library for our 3rd year Sensors course. We created a crow-shaped controller to control a crow on screen with the goal of bringing items back to its nest. The Arduino UNO controller has an IR sensor underneath to detect height, a pressure sensor in each wing to allow players to hold and carry items, a button on each wing to flip the crow's direction on screen, and an RGB LED as each eye to indicate various states within the game.

Image.alt: Players are tasked with picking up items of various 'weights' and returning them to their nest to gather points.
The crow on screen detects the height of the controller.
The controller is powered by an Arduino UNO, and the casing is created with cardboard, plastic squeeze bottles, foam and black tape.
